memo_delta.summary: Thirty days into the Watchlist call, price action is immaterial (+1.06% vs. the S&P 500's -0.24%) and none of the five forecast-ledger items or five red-flag-linked risks has resolved -- the thesis remains exactly where it was, correctly classified as too early to grade. The one genuinely new fact is a securities-fraud class action (filed/publicized 2026-08-25 through 2026-09-04, lead-plaintiff deadline 2026-10-13) alleging non-disclosure of OWYN integration and pea-protein sourcing issues during 2024-10-24 to 2026-04-08 -- a legal escalation of the already-flagged RF-CAP-004/RF-DISC-002 Critical red flags, not new underlying business information.
memo_delta.stage_one_comment: Simply Good Foods is basically flat since our August 6 Watchlist call -- up about 1%, in line with a roughly flat S&P 500 over the same month. Nothing in the thesis has actually been tested yet: the decisive event is the October 23 earnings print, which will show whether the company stayed inside its own guidance and whether a fourth straight quarter of write-downs shows up, and that has not happened yet. The one new development is that shareholders have filed a securities-fraud lawsuit over the OWYN acquisition, alleging the company hid integration and product-quality problems before the big write-down earlier this year. This is not new information about the business -- we already knew about and flagged those OWYN problems -- but the formal lawsuit itself is a new, and modestly negative, layer of legal and distraction risk sitting on top of the Critical red flag that already caps this at Watchlist. We are not changing the rating. The next real test is the October 23 print.
